description: Seeded agent case: an n8n Agent the conversation already built is restored (config + one skill) and the live turn asks for a second skill. Tests that the assistant CONTINUES the existing agent rather than building a new one — the failure mode a seeded agent case exists to catch — and that the original skill survives the edit. Build-only; graded on the rendered agent artifact.

config.name: Support Triage
config.instructions: You triage inbound customer support tickets. Read the ticket, decide how urgent it is, and reply to the customer with what happens next.

skill_triage_rules.name: Triage rules
skill_triage_rules.description: How to assign a severity to an inbound ticket
skill_triage_rules.instructions:
Assign every ticket exactly one severity.

- **P1** — the customer cannot use the product at all, or data is at risk.
- **P2** — a core feature is broken but there is a workaround.
- **P3** — everything else: questions, cosmetic issues, feature requests.

State the severity in your reply to the customer, in plain language rather than the P-number.

processExpectations: The assistant edited the EXISTING Support Triage agent — it did not create a second, separate agent for the refund escalation.
outcomeExpectations: The Support Triage agent has a skill covering refund escalation: anything mentioning a refund goes to the billing team, and the reply to the customer says the ticket was escalated to billing.
The original 'Triage rules' skill is still attached to the agent and still describes the P1/P2/P3 severity levels — the refund change was added alongside it, not in place of it.
The agent's instructions still describe triaging inbound support tickets — the agent was edited, not rebuilt from scratch as something else.
